newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican farmers take out product 'put' options.
newsitem.headline: Mexican farmers take out product 'put' options.

text.p: Mexican farmers are being eased into the world of put options as insurance against crop failure or failing physical prices, the Agriculture Ministry said in a report obtained Friday.
Last year the ministry began its Farm Products Price Options Program for corn, wheat, soybean and cotton growers to buy options with the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
Up to fourth-quarter 1996, Mexican farmers had placed 874 put options for wheat covering 118,933 tonnes of product. For cotton, 753 puts had been made, covering 17,078 tonnes, the ministry said.
